_comment: Release gates, enforced by scripts/lint_release_gates.py (read its docstring for every rule). A version at or above a gate's key fails CI until every item and arm is satisfied (evidence + a red gate for an item; the golden key + direct-assertion evidence for an arm) or retired, every gated function is unpinned and at most max_lines, and every baseline entry outside debt_snapshot has an accepted_new_debt record. Entries are never removed or reworded: retired and accepted_new_debt are append-only. The diff that raises the version across a gate may not change this file.

1.4.0.source: Owner decision 2026-10-15: 1.3.2 ships without the rest of the agent_loop/orchestrator decomposition, and no version >= 1.4.0 passes CI until it is done. Design: the 2026-10-15 approach note and adversarial pass (SF-1..SF-11), as folded by its review (2026-10-15); docs/plans/roadmap_1_4.md §Release thresholds T0.

functions.why: The orchestrator decomposition (roadmap_1_3_x.md item 7); pinned at 3003 at slice 0 (#1269).
The agent_loop decomposition (roadmap_1_3_x.md item 7, slices 0-5 merged).
Split out of run_agentic_loop by #1133; its own split is #1150. Gated with its split-outs (owner decision 2026-10-15, SF-6).

required.scope: An adopted persistent_agent arm: the HANDLE seam's branches 3 and 4 (no session AUT snapshot, the tool-lease restore, the DefaultNetwork pain-bridge unsubscribe), owed before the slice that moves §13 teardown or §14 report/save (roadmap_1_3_x.md, orchestrator slice 0 review 2026-10-13).
An imagination-enabled arm reaching §7 (the ImaginationTrigger wiring and its teardown), owed before the teardown/report slices.
A /new arm: the post-sim reader faked to return a goal, so the run re-enters start_simulation_mode; owed before the teardown/report slices.
A stall-detector arm that reaches the detector's injections (past its first diversity checkpoint and its idle threshold), owed before the slice that moves §11.
A generative-campaign arm (generative=True) pinning that the generative campaign sets stop_event before the §9 resume/kickoff injection reaches the narrator.

items.scope: finish_simulation ends the run: once the narrator finishes, the run stops without waiting out the source's 180 s exhaustion grace, and the stall detector does not nudge a narrator that has finished.
/pause is a state the dispatch path enforces, not a percept the narrator is asked to obey: while a run is paused, no narrator send_message reaches the agent under test.
#1263 part 1: no plan-logger or plan-dashboard writer thread started by a sim's agents outlives that sim's teardown (each writer has an owner that stops it).
#1263 part 1: the MemoryAgent memctx_* context pool has an owner that shuts it down; no memctx thread a run started is left running by teardown.
#1263 part 2: run_agentic_loop's teardown runs on every exit path, including a loop that raises, so a DefaultNetwork the loop started is stopped even when the loop fails.
#1263 part 3: DefaultNetwork.start() after stop() restores the bus subscription stop() removed, so a restarted DefaultNetwork with a bus is not deaf.
#1263's DefaultNetwork part: the loop stops the DefaultNetwork it started, in sim mode too (#1281). Ships in #1260; its evidence is that PR's red gate once it is on main.

ConceptExtractor worker threads are stopped by their owner; none outlive the test or sim that started them (#1263 part, owner decision 2026-10-15). Site: memory/concept_extractor.py::ConceptExtractor._worker_loop (about 123 still alive at the end of a fast unit run, #1281 evidence).
The agent-under-test and narrator loops of one sim never share a runtime state path or its temp file.
A sim report's lane_breakdown and latency percentiles count only that session's LLM calls, never an earlier sim's in the same process.
The interactive sim's SIGTERM terminal-restore handler is actually installed (from a thread that can install it), and SIGTERM restores the saved terminal settings.
The orchestrator's set_entity_sensor guidance does not advertise health, which no shipped body can write.
The orchestrator's set_entity_sensor guidance does not state a fixed 0.0-1.0 range; value mode clamps each sensor to its declared range (signed sensors are [-1, 1]).
set_entity_sensor's schema no longer silently defaults value to 1.0 when a call gives neither value nor delta.
The orchestrator's --resume-sim lookup goes through utils/paths.py::resolve_run_dir: an unknown session id is an error, and the lookup creates no directory.

runtime/tool_dispatch.py::execute_and_learn adds a turn to conversation history by Tool.speech_params (the executor's registry), not by a list of speech-tool names, so say and a body's speech affordance enter it. modes/definitions.py::CORE_TOOLS is exempt: it is a mode-membership list that gates which tools a mode offers, not a reader of what was said (owner decision 2026-10-15).

agents/exec_agent.py::ExecAgent.deliberate decides a SpeakIntent by Tool.speech_params, not by the speak_tools name set. modes/definitions.py::CORE_TOOLS is exempt: it is a mode-membership list that gates which tools a mode offers, not a reader of what was said (owner decision 2026-10-15).

The orchestrator's stall nudge (start_simulation_mode's _build_stall_nudge_example) picks its 'you have spoken' text from ActionRecord.utterance or Tool.speech_params, not a list of speech-tool names. modes/definitions.py::CORE_TOOLS is exempt: it is a mode-membership list that gates which tools a mode offers, not a reader of what was said (owner decision 2026-10-15).

console/handle.py::TALK_CONVERSATIONAL_TOOLS no longer names the speech tools in a literal list: talk()'s speech tools are derived from Tool.speech_params. modes/definitions.py::CORE_TOOLS is exempt: it is a mode-membership list that gates which tools a mode offers, not a reader of what was said (owner decision 2026-10-15).
A follow-up's tool result travels as the typed ActionFollowup on its own field, not as synthetic text in cli_inputs; cli_inputs holds only human input.

The RPE a goal's staging significance reads belongs to that goal: a goal with no NAc update of its own does not read an earlier, unrelated surprise, and a first-time link's surprise is the one recorded. The binding is decided in its PR.
#845 item 1: the replan prompt's prior-attempts section renders from real episodes (runtime/loop_state.py::_extract_episode_actions reads fields real episodes carry).
Either wire a true per-turn internet policy summary (from the live getter, each sentence enforced) into the prompt, or delete the dead fields end to end (decided in its PR).

items.source: These orchestrator sites WIDEN #863 beyond its own scan, which excluded simulation/; they are enumerated here by the owner's decision of 2026-10-15. Found by an AST scan of src/maxim/simulation/orchestrator.py at b4c2ea88 (a broad try whose body calls a sim_logger sim_* function, the innermost such try owning the call) and classified by #863's 2026-09-24 DROP/KEEP rule, not the 2026-09-23 argument criterion: DROP = the try guards only an emit whose arguments cannot raise (since #868 the wrap does nothing); KEEP = it guards real, fallible or state-changing caller logic (out of #863's scope). Only DROP-class sites are gated. KEEP-class, not gated: the enable_sim_logging wrap (it mutates the logger's global state; not an emitter, so outside DROP) and the disable_sim_logging wrap (it mutates that state and can raise on _log_file.close(); not an emitter) and the scene-manifest pre-trigger block (it guards generate_scene_manifest, an LLM call, and process_manifest, which changes state). Also not gated: display_status wraps (display calls wait for a display contract, #863 comment 2026-09-24), the get_interactive_mode wrap (a getter) and the sim_agent_context wraps (a context manager that sets the agent contextvar), none of them emitters; and #863's aside on explicit-form handlers (comment 2026-09-23, not in its close condition). Deciding reason for this site: DROP: every guarded statement is a @_contained sim_log emit or the construction of its message from typed reads (the tool-name sets, EntityMap.list_entities(), Entity.name/entity_type, Modulator.affordances keys); nothing changes state and nothing in the payload can raise.

items.scope: #1305: no module under src/maxim/default_network/, src/maxim/attention/ or src/maxim/spatial/, nor src/maxim/decisions/significance.py, draws from a process-global generator (a call to a function of the stdlib random module, or to numpy's legacy np.random.* functions such as np.random.choice). Each draws from an owned generator instance (random.Random or numpy.random.Generator) whose seed derives from the seed utils/seeding.py::seed_all last set (utils/seeding.py::get_global_seed). So a draw in those modules does not advance the process-global streams, and a thread drawing there cannot disturb a seed-then-draw on another thread; after seed_all(s), the same calls on objects constructed after it yield the same draws.
items.source: #1305 (filed 2026-10-15), split from #1281's fix (a) when #1281 closed: PR #1299 removed the flake's cause (the leaked DefaultNetwork) and a 2026-10-15 probe found no leaked global draws, so what remains is seeded reproducibility (global random drawn on concurrent threads, e.g. significance._random_init on the Minecraft AUT thread). Owner decision 2026-10-15: it stays a 1.4.0 gate item.

items.scope: #1263's thread guard (#1281's fix (b)): a tests/conftest.py guard fails any fast-suite test for which a loop thread that appeared while the test or its fixtures ran (a thread whose target is a *_run_loop, *_writer_loop or *_worker_loop method, or a memctx_* pool worker) is still alive once the fixtures that started it have been torn down; its allowlist is empty.
